label: The Legendre Transform
notes: Open by framing the lecture as a bridge: mechanics on the tangent bundle uses velocities, but symplectic geometry lives on the cotangent bundle and uses momenta. The Legendre transform is the convex-analytic device that carries us across, and we will build it carefully from strict convexity upward.

label: Strict Convexity
notes: Stress that strict convexity is the local engine. A positive-definite Hessian makes every tangent hyperplane a strict support of the graph and makes the gradient map locally injective. Warn that this is purely local information; it certifies invertibility near a point, not yet a global change of coordinates.

label: Stability Set
notes: Introduce the stability set as the global complement to the local picture. A slope is stable only when the tilted function keeps a genuine proper minimum, and the set of such slopes is exactly the image of the gradient map. Use the exponential example to show convexity without full stability.

label: The Legendre Map
notes: Define the fiber derivative as velocity to momentum, sending a vector to the differential of the Lagrangian in that vector. Under fiberwise strict convexity this map is a diffeomorphism from the tangent space onto the stability set, with the inverse recovering velocity from momentum by solving the gradient equation.

label: The Dual Function
notes: Present the convex conjugate as a supremum of linear minus convex. Explain that the supremum is attained where the slope of the Lagrangian equals the chosen momentum, so the dual value is read off the supporting line. The conjugate is always convex, even when the primal barely is.

label: Young-Fenchel Inequality
notes: State the Young inequality and emphasize the equality case, which is the whole point. The gap between the sum of dual values and the pairing is nonnegative and vanishes exactly along the graph of the Legendre map. This equality curve is the certificate that the transform is exact.

label: From TM to T*M
notes: Lift the construction to bundles. Applying the fiber derivative on each tangent space simultaneously gives a global map from the tangent bundle to the cotangent bundle covering the identity on the base. Fiberwise convexity guarantees it is a diffeomorphism, so momentum coordinates replace velocity coordinates everywhere.

label: The Hamiltonian
notes: Build the Hamiltonian as the conjugate of the Lagrangian taken fiberwise, the supremum of momentum paired with velocity minus the Lagrangian. Walk through the worked mechanical model where momentum is mass times velocity and the Hamiltonian becomes kinetic energy in momentum form plus potential energy.

label: Euler-Lagrange to Hamilton
notes: Show the payoff: under the Legendre transform the second-order Euler-Lagrange equations become Hamilton's first-order system. The two chain-rule identities, partial H by partial momentum equals velocity and partial H by partial position equals minus the Lagrangian derivative, do the entire conversion exactly.

label: Convex Duality Picture
notes: Tie the threads together with the supporting-line picture. The Lagrangian and Hamiltonian are Legendre duals: each is the envelope of tangent lines whose slopes and intercepts encode the other. Reflecting slopes and values across this construction is the geometric content of the whole transform.

label: Summary
notes: Recap the dependency chain from positive Hessian to stability to diffeomorphism to dual function to Hamilton's equations. Remind students that convexity is the load-bearing hypothesis; if it fails the fiber map stops being invertible and the Hamiltonian picture breaks down. Preview cotangent dynamics ahead.
